title: Pydantic validation error when using custom settings
body:
Hi! Thank you for fixes, now importing filename from config name works fine. However, another issue is raised, when I am trying to set myself a custom config. For example:
```python3
from paperqa.settings import (
    AgentSettings,
    AnswerSettings,
    IndexSettings,
    ParsingSettings,
    PromptSettings,
    Settings,
)
settings=Settings(
    AnswerSettings(
        evidence_k=10,
        evidence_detailed_citations=True,
        evidence_retrieval=True,
        evidence_summary_length="about 100 words",
        evidence_skip_summary=False,
        answer_max_sources=5,
        max_answer_attempts=None,
        answer_length="must not exceed 1000 words, but sometimes can be longer",
        max_concurrent_requests=10,
    )
)
```

Raises this pydantic error:
```
ValidationError: 1 validation error for AnswerSettings
evidence_detailed_citations
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value=True, input_type=bool]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.12/v/extra_forbidden
```

Also put it as comment in the PR: https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/pull/1251#issuecomment-3686104549

comments.author: dosubot
comments.text:
<!-- Answer -->
The error happens because Pydantic models in paper-qa use strict validation (`extra="forbid"`), so any field not defined in the model schema will trigger a validation error. However, `evidence_detailed_citations` is a valid field in the current `AnswerSettings` model—so if you see it flagged as "extra," it usually means your code and installed package are out of sync, or you might be passing arguments incorrectly.

Make sure you are instantiating `Settings` with keyword arguments for each nested settings class, like this:

```python
settings = Settings(
    answer=AnswerSettings(
        evidence_k=10,
        evidence_detailed_citations=True,
        # ... other fields ...
    )
)
```

If you pass an `AnswerSettings` instance as a positional argument to `Settings`, Pydantic may misinterpret it and cause validation errors.

If you still get the error, check that your installed `paper-qa` package and your code are both up to date, especially after recent config/schema changes ([see PR #1251](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/pull/1251)). If you have custom config files, make sure they only include fields currently accepted by the model—remove any deprecated or extra fields to match the latest schema. This pattern of strict validation and config drift has caused similar issues before ([example](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/issues/1250), [model definition](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/blob/8221e3cf8b7ff7b2485cd9e05e44387dab183a0a/paperqa/settings.py#L70-L129)).
